goal: Make Pi the sole supported code-agent host for Immune-Brain by removing every Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode installation, adapter, configuration, release, and current-documentation surface while preserving the Pi package, Pi extension authority, shared runtime and Kernel behavior required by Pi, provider-agnostic model selection inside Pi, and immutable historical records.

acceptance.assertion: The shipped and public package exposes only the root Pi package manifest, Pi skills, Pi extensions, and Pi-required runtime files; Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode manifests, marketplaces, adapters, package dependencies, exports, and release artifacts are absent.

Production host routing accepts only Pi for local configuration, advisory dispatch, work probes, and completion metadata, with no non-Pi tool-envelope branch or generic unknown-host fallback; Pi may still select model IDs from any configured model provider.
Versioning, release, install checks, public synchronization, and package validation derive from the Pi package boundary and cannot require, publish, copy, or recreate a non-Pi host surface.

Current README, user guides, reference docs, Skill contracts, packaged dist artifacts, registry metadata, architecture map, and ADR guidance describe Pi as the only supported code-agent host, while historical Plans, Specs, archives, and Learnings remain retained as historical evidence rather than rewritten compatibility claims.

Pi installation, Skill discovery, isolated Agent subagents, progress projection, TUI canary enrollment and lifecycle authority, verification descriptor execution, Kernel storage, and package registry contracts continue to pass after the non-Pi support removal.
